subject: Architecture
title: Cable-Stayed Bridges: Modern Elegance
description: A quick win: understand Cable-Stayed Bridges: Modern Elegance.

hook.text: Cable-stayed bridges look like suspension bridges but work completely differently.

buildup.text: Cables run directly from tower to deck in straight lines — no main cable draping between towers.

discovery.text: This makes them stiffer than suspension bridges and better at resisting wind-induced movement.

twist.text: Cable-stayed bridges can be built from both ends simultaneously — no temporary supports needed below.

climax.text: The Millau Viaduct in France stands taller than the Eiffel Tower — 1,125 feet at its highest point.

punchline.text: They look like harps made of steel. And they play beautifully.

quiz.question: How do cable-stayed bridges differ from suspension bridges?
options: Cables run directly from tower to deck instead of draping between towers
They use concrete cables instead of steel
They can only span short distances over rivers
